content:
This item had been deferred from the previous
meeting on 12th March 2026. Before the item was
presented, the Assistant Director (Planning) informed the Committee
that the application would be presented in full, due to the new
Members of the Committee following Annual Council. The Committee
were made aware that the discussion on grey belt would not be
covered in the same level of detail, as it is covered in the
Officer’s report. The Committee were also informed that they
were not bound by the resolution of the previous meeting.
 
The Committee received a report that sought
outline planning permission for the erection of up to 60 dwellings
(use Class C3) with all matters reserved except for access.
 
Erik Pagano, agent for the application,
addressed the Committee as follows:
 
“Good
evening, my name is Erik Pagano and I represent Landform Estates,
the promoter of the Bulls Lane site. This high-quality project will
deliver 60 new homes, including 30 affordable homes, all set within
an exceptional urban and landscape design. Over half of the site is
dedicated to new public open space, achieving a notable
biodiversity net gain of over 38%.
 
Following questions
at the 12th of March committee meeting, I have checked the details
of our technical team and the Council's statutory consultees, all
of whom have no objection to the proposals, and I can confirm the
following. There is no evidence of badgers, otters, water voles,
amphibians, or any other notable species on site or in the nearby
brook, as the habitat is suboptimal for them. All trees with bat
roosting potential will be retained, and together with new planting
and bat boxes, their habitat will in fact be enhanced. Existing
trees and hedges will also be improved to encourage nesting and
foraging birds. The site is underlain by land of clay and gravels,
with no chalk, sinkholes or contamination, allowing for standard
foundation designs. The Environment Agency has confirmed that all
homes sit within Flood Zone 1, the lowest
risk category.
 
Furthermore,
Hertfordshire County Council Highways has approved the widening of
Bulls Lane, new road drainage, a new footpath and cycleway, and
various nearby highway and bus stop improvements. In addition to
the standard CIL payments, the Section 1 agreement secures a
separate £50,000 contribution to the nearby North
Mymms Youth and Community Centre to
help fund its modernisation and enhanced community use. There are
no technical impediments preventing the successful delivery of this
site and the Section 106 agreement has been prepared and is ready
to sign. This means that should members resolve to approve the
proposals this evening,
that development
can commence in the short term. In the time available Mr Chairman,
I hope this summary has adequately addressed the questions
previously raised and I commend this proposal to members. Thank
you.”
 
 
Thomas Squire, spoke against the application,
addressed the Committee as follows:
 
“Good evening
Chair and Committee Members. I'm speaking on behalf of Welham Green
residents standing side by side with the Campaign to Protect Rural
England and the North Mymms Green Belt
Society opposing this application. In March this Committee chose
common sense by not approving this flawed application. Since then
our village has united under the Save the Horsefields campaign. Our
petition gained over 1300 signatures, that's half of Welham Green.
And our residents also crowdfunded independent planning and
ecologist reports.
The planning report
by Barker-Parry confirms this application remains deeply flawed.
Culling of veteran trees, direct violation of NPPF paragraph 193,
foul drainage, echoing Thames Waters' own damming report,
neighbouring amenities, failing to consider existing properties and
the Grade II listed farmhouse violating local plan policy SADM 10
and transport impacts. I would go as far to say that this site has
the worst access of any proposed site in the area. 1 .6 by the
railway bridge which narrows to 4 .2 meters can only be single
file. The other is a dangerous seven access junction. Combined with
local proposals, the community of traffic creates a significant
impact that cannot be cost effectively managed, meeting the
threshold for refusal under NPPF paragraph 115. You cannot approve
this outline application with these issues unresolved.
 
Next wildlife, the
applicants claim ecological impacts are negligible. They are wrong.
We have submitted community evidence proving the presence of
protected bats, newts, badgers and rare birds that I sent to the
Committee two days ago. This is backed by independent ecologist
reports, which states critical questions remain unanswered and
stringent mitigation measures are required before development can
begin. Furthermore, this is inappropriate development of green
belt, harmful by definition. The land is London Metropolitan Green
belt and is not included in the adopted local plan. It forms a
strategic gap, preventing urban sprawl. Developing it means a
permanent loss of openness.
 
Finally, heritage.
This development will cause permanent harm to Grade II listed
Skimpands Farm and its intact 18th
century Georgian landscape. In August 1800, the Times described
this very site as “the house and lands are wholly meadow, so
beautiful, disposed, and enriched with noble oak and other timber
trees, shrubberies, and springs. It can be formed into one of the
most choice residences in the county of Hertford.” This was
226 years ago. This is the epitome of local heritage, not to
mention the ancient artefacts found on the site, as confirmed by
the British Museum.
 
In conclusion, the
public benefit of 60 houses is completely dwarfed by the
destruction of historic pasture and green belt. Please listen to
the CPRE, Green Belt Society and the independent experts and to the
1300 residents who stand against this. To prevent the green from
being permanently lost in Welham Green, we urge you to reject this
application. Thank you.” 
 
Councillor Mia Americanos-Molinaro, North
Mymms Parish Council, addressed the
Committee as follows:
 
“Thank you
chair. NMPC stance is that the attempted designation of grey belt
status for this parcel of land was wrong, we agree with you. This
is genuine green belt land with no very special circumstances
permitting development. There has been a misapplication of policy,
mischaracterization of harm and overstatement of benefits by the
developers.
 
This site lies
immediately adjacent to Skimpands Farm,
a Grade II, listed heritage asset and the council's own consultants
confirm that the land continues to make a positive contribution to
its setting. The presence of a designated heritage asset is a
strong reason for restricting development and having no grey belt
status the land forms part of this historic setting. Yes,
mitigation was offered by the developer. It may reduce harm, but it
does not remove the footnote 7 trigger so the approach is flawed.
We believe harm to the green belt has been very understated.
Officers repeatedly describe the harm as being at the lower end of
substantial weight because the site is visually contained but the
NPPF is explicit. Any harm to the green belt, spatial or visual,
must be given substantial weight. This is open pasture land forming
part of the countryside and the introduction of 60 dwellings and
roads, etc, is pure encroachment directly conflicting with green
belt purposes and this is downplaying the harm. This land makes a
very strong contribution to green belt purposes. It preserves a
historic setting, prevents urban sprawl, supports much wildlife and
ecology with openness and character. The proposal has overstated
the benefits and wrongly treated normal policy compliance as very
special circumstances. Housing need cannot in itself amount to VSC.
The NPPF is unequivocal on this. There's heavy reliance on whether
Hatfield's housing supply deficit, but this site was not allocated
in the local plan, even though the inspector was aware of the
shortfall.
 
That of the
material consideration waned strongly against the developer’s
VSC argument. The developers push their BNG, public access and
sustainability measures, but these aren't exceptional benefits,
they're standard requirements, so they can't outweigh green belt
harm. Ironically, they hope to achieve BNG by putting hedges on
water courses, whilst our community is trying to preserve the
existing habitats of bats, badgers, rare birds, as well as feeding
several horses. Developers propose green areas for kids, but their
green spaces are fraught with the danger from construction and
resident traffic on narrow country roads.
 
Development on this
parcel would harm openness, visual amenity and character. There'd
be harms of encroachment into the countryside, settlement sprawl
and urbanising of the village with worsening of our flooding and
drainage problems. The developer relies on minimising harm and
inflating benefits, but the position is clear.  Green belt harm carries substantial weight.
Presumption in favour of development no longer applies where there
are protected assets and places and the developer’s benefits
are routine; they don't meet the VSC thresholds. Had this been grey
belt we would still have asked you to look at the function of this
land where green belt purposes are fulfilled. In the planning
balance the harms aren't outweighed and with no very special
circumstances, we respectfully ask that the application be refused
thank you”
 
Councillor Bonfante addressed the Committee as
follows:
 
“Thank you
Chair and thank you to Members and especially welcome to the new
Members of this Committee, as well as Members of the Public who
have taken the time to brave the heat to join us today.
 
And just to speak
to members, I understand the position you are in. I was on the same
training courses you were when it comes to this. I understand you
need a defensible position here. And I'm here to assure you that
there is one available.
 
As previously
mentioned, there is a Grade II listed building. In the council's
own heritage consultants, it mentions that while the officers state
less than substantial harm, that is still harm. And if harm is
attributed to a heritage asset, that triggers footnote 7 of the
NPPF, which prevents it from being designated as grey belt. This
proposed development causes harm onto a heritage asset, which
triggers footnote 7 of the NPPF, making it inappropriate to be
classified as grey belt.
 
I know on the
agenda you see stuff on mitigation measures and hedges and orchards
and stuff like that. I am dubious to say the least. I think how
many times has this committee seen applications that have said this
but down the road it gets cut away, especially with local
government reorganisation on our tails. This is the kind of stuff
that gets left on the cutting room floor. What if the flooding
issue causes more troubles?
What if the
sinkholes are more trouble than they're worth? What if access
becomes more challenging to deal with? What if damage to the
wildlife becomes more significant? What if the archaeological team
digs up old English king? What if then?
What if those
changes will have an impact on the financial reality of the
development and these mitigation measures fall to the wayside?
 
I know we're in a
housing shortfall. I understand that. But we've got to make sure
the housing that is in Welwyn Hatfield for our residents, past,
present and future, is appropriate and is appropriate to sustain a
home, not just bricks and roofs, a real home for the future members
of our Borough. And that simply cannot be accomplished here.
 
And I'd like to
make this very, very clear that the agenda set out for you states
that harm will be exhibited onto a Grade II listed building. If a
Grade II listed building exhibits harm, footnote 7 of the NPPF
applies. If footnote 7 of the NPPF applies, the land could not be
considered grey belt. If the land could not be considered grey
belt, it must be considered green belt. And if it's considered
green belt, then there is a justifiable and defensible position to
be able to reject this.
 
I urge members of
this committee to protect our green belt, protect what makes the
identity of not just Welham Green, but Welwyn Hatfield, the special
place that it is.
That's what we all
got elected to do. And I hope you make the same decision this
committee made in March. Have a wonderful day and stay cool. Thank
you.”
 
The following points were raised during the
discussion:

·       
A Member raised a question on the outline element of the
application and what could be considered at this Committee. The
Head of Development Management Servies confirmed that the outline
application set out the developable areas, with 57% of the site
being open space, allowing the mitigation and protection of the
setting of the listed building.

·       
Clarification was sought regarding the ecological impact on the
land, as differing values had been presented by the Speakers. The
Head of Development Management Services responded that the ecology
reports had been assessed by Hertfordshire County Council and a
response of no objection had been received from the experts.

·       
A Member commented on the nature of the single lane access to the
site under the railway bridge. The Head of Development Management
Services responded that as Hertfordshire County Council raised no
objections to the scheme and a Construction Management Plan was
attached, officers had no concerns regarding the scheme.

·       
Clarification was sought regarding if any trees on site were
subject to Tree Protection orders. Officers confirmed there were no
TPOs on site.

·       
A Member raised a question regarding the scheme detailing up to 60
dwellings and whether the number would increase in a subsequent
application. The Head of Development Management Services informed
Members that if the outline application were approved, 60 dwellings
would be the maximum.

·       
Clarification was sought regarding the legal implications for the
proposed management company and how it would function over the
site. The Head of Development Management Services replied that it
was a common management structure for new housing developments, and
that the Section 106 agreement would secure safeguards to ensure
that the management company was fit for purpose.

·       
A comment was made regarding the non-adoption of roads by
Hertfordshire County Council.

·       
Clarification was sought on the measures proposed to mitigate any
green belt harm. Officers responded that future reserved matter
applications would have to restrict development to the 43% of the
site allocated as such, which allowed the development to be stood
back from the listed building and its setting.

·       
A Member commented on the risks of appeal and asked for
clarification on the potential of costs being awarded against the
Council. The Assistant Director (Planning) replied that when a
committee refuses the officer recommendation, there is a
requirement for a strong defensible planning reason. The Committee
were also informed that there would be a cost involved in defending
an appeal from third party defence, due to officer’s positive
views on the application, and that the Inspector may award costs
against the Council.

·       
A Member commented on the need to represent residents, balanced
with an equal need to avoid wasting their money.

·       
Members received legal advice regarding the late submissions from
objectors sent to Members in advance of the Committee but which had
not been sent to Officers. The Committee was advised by the Head of
Development Management Services that officers would need to
consider the late submissions and seek comments from Hertfordshire
Ecology after the meeting Legal advice recommended that any
positive decision made on this application should be subject to
consideration by officers of the further submissions received and
consultation with relevant consultees. The resolution could
stipulate that officers should re-present the application to
Committee if the submissions raised new material consideration.

·       
A Member commented on the archaeology clause and asked for
clarification from officers. Officers confirmed that the
recommendation from Hertfordshire County Council that no
development would commence until a written scheme had been
submitted and approved was included.

·       
Clarification was sought on the risk of loss of planning authority
due to breaking the threshold of overturned appeals. The Assistant
Director (Planning) informed the Committee of the 10% benchmark of
appeals for major applications being overturned. The Committee were
reminded that this was the reason that strong, defendable planning
reasons were needed for the Committee to go against an officer
recommendation.

·       
A Member commented on the balance and requested clarification. The
Assistant Director (Planning) informed the Committee that not all
items were equally weighted with the planning balance, and it was
for the Committee to determine the balancing exercise.

·       
The Committee were informed that officers had to apply the NPPF as
written, and therefore the green belt purpose of preventing a large
built-up area did not apply to Welham Green.

·       
A Member commented on the topography of the land towards the
heritage asset and raised a question regarding how it impacted
decision making. Officers responded that topography had been fully
considered and included within the Place Services assessment of the
potential harm to the listed building. 

·       
A Member raised a question on whether an Inspector would consider
the grey belt argument or if they would accept the
Committee’s view on grey belt. The Assistant Director
(Planning) responded that the inspector would consider the site as
a whole and determine whether the site sits as grey belt.
 
Resolved:
(for 5, against 4, abstain 0)
To approve the grant of planning permission
subject to the conditions and section 106 planning obligations set
out in the report and subject to officers being satisfied, in
consultation with the Chair, that no new material considerations
arise from the late evidence submitted to Members prior to the
meeting.    
 
NOTE – Councillors Goldwater and Hobbs
arrived late to the meeting during this item and therefore did not
take part in the voting on this item.
